synthesis.evidence_balance: mixed — a cash-generative IG-rated core with real AI booking momentum set against genuine GAAP-loss, heavy leverage, and sharp forward-estimate cuts.

bull_points.claim: Absolute EBITDA has held/risen even as the margin % dipped — LTM EBITDA $1,275M vs FY24 $1,295M and FY23 $1,045M on a rising revenue base ($9,999M LTM), so the 13% margin is optical compression, not collapsing earnings power.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement (margin % + absolute EBITDA reconciler)

bull_points.claim: The business is FCF-positive at $775.6M LTM and buying back stock (-5.9% shares over ~1.7y), consistent with a self-funding profile rather than a distressed one.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Cash Flow 'Levered Free Cash Flow' [LTM 12 months May-31-2026]

bull_points.claim: S&P issuer rating is BBB-, investment grade, with credit-health scores 4/4/4/4 flagged against a peer-median 3/3/3/3 — leverage is elevated but the name still carries an IG rating.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Credit Health Panel · as-of 2026-06-25

bull_points.claim: Interest coverage is 4.6x EBITDA/interest, indicating the debt load is currently serviced out of operating earnings.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement EBITDA ÷ Interest Expense [LTM 12 months May-31-2026]

bull_points.claim: Forward-facing demand indicators are constructive: signed AI annual contract value more than doubled QoQ and technology wins were up more than 61% year-over-year in Q1 2026.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Concentrix Corporation, Q1 2026 Earnings Call, Mar 24, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Growth verticals are still expanding in constant currency — banking and financial services grew 13% year-over-year in Q1 2026, offsetting weaker verticals.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Concentrix Corporation, Q1 2026 Earnings Call, Mar 24, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: On a forward basis the name trades at NTM TEV/EBITDA 4.54x vs peer-median 5.26x, but this peer set spans $103M–$32.0B (311x) caps and differing models, so whether that gap is EARNED (name margin 12% vs peer 17%, EBITDA growth -4% vs 0%, leverage 3.4x vs 2.0x) or RESIDUAL/overshoot is for the human to judge, not a clean 'cheap' signal.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Operating Statistics (name vs peer median: growth/margin/leverage/beta)

bear_points.claim: GAAP net income swung to a large loss (FY25 -$1,279M, LTM -$1,314M) driving RoE to -37.7% and rendering the P/E NM — earnings power on a GAAP basis has genuinely broken, not merely optically dipped.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Ratios (RoE / RoCE / RoA + leverage, multi-year columns)

bear_points.claim: Leverage is heavy and above peers: net-debt/EBITDA 4.1x and total-debt/EBITDA 3.4x vs peer-median 2.0x; management's own target of below 2.6x by end-FY26 signals the current level is a problem being actively worked down.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Net Debt $5,249M [Q2 May-31-2026] ÷ CIQ EBITDA $1,275M [LTM 12 months May-31-2026]

bear_points.claim: On the company-adjusted EBITDA basis ($368.7M) net leverage triangulates to ~14.2x — a far worse read than the CIQ GAAP-basis 4.1x, and this is the REAL signal the CIQ multiple understates, not a misread.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ leverage bases + release LTM adj-EBITDA/margins

bear_points.claim: The consensus earnings path has been cut sharply: FY26 GAAP EPS revised from 6.09 to 4.00 (-34%) and GAAP net income -36% over 12m, so the de-rate tracks genuine forward-estimate deterioration, not just sentiment.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (current-FY consensus path; ragged, absent lookbacks n/a)

bear_points.claim: ROIC has structurally declined from 9.0% (FY22) to 4.2% LTM, below any plausible cost of capital on this leverage, indicating value-destructive capital deployment through the Webhelp-scale expansion.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Ratios (Return on Capital %, multi-year columns)

bear_points.claim: The de-rate is idiosyncratic, not market-driven: CNXC fell -45.4% over 180d while the small-cap benchmark rose +17.0%, a -62.4% relative move — the market is pricing a company-specific problem.

Core verticals are contracting: technology/consumer-electronics and health care each fell about 6% in constant currency on lighter client volumes and shore mix, the AI-disruption thesis the bears fear.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Concentrix Corporation, Q1 2026 Earnings Call, Mar 24, 2026.rtf

decisive_question.question: Is CNXC's cash-generative, IG-rated core mean-reverting through an AI-driven mix transition (overshoot), or is AI structurally eroding the high-volume CX/BPO base faster than the higher-value pivot can replace it, leaving a value-destructive levered balance sheet (terminal)?

evidence_for.claim: AI-linked bookings momentum is real — signed AI annual contract value more than doubled QoQ and technology wins rose more than 61% year-over-year, suggesting the pivot is landing.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Concentrix Corporation, Q1 2026 Earnings Call, Mar 24, 2026.rtf

evidence_for.claim: Absolute LTM EBITDA ($1,275M) and FCF ($775.6M) remain robust on a rising revenue base, so the cash engine funding the transition is intact.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Cash Flow 'Levered Free Cash Flow' [LTM 12 months May-31-2026]

evidence_against.claim: The verticals most exposed to automation — technology/consumer-electronics and health care — are already shrinking about 6% in constant currency on lighter volumes, the leading edge of structural erosion.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Concentrix Corporation, Q1 2026 Earnings Call, Mar 24, 2026.rtf

evidence_against.claim: Consensus FY26 GAAP EPS was cut -34% and net income -36% over 12 months while ROIC sits at 4.2% — forward earnings are deteriorating against a leveraged capital base.
evidence_against.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (current-FY consensus path; ragged, absent lookbacks n/a)

key_unknowns: Adjusted forward EV/EBITDA and adjusted EPS are not in the revised guidance — with company-adjusted EBITDA (~$368.7M) implying ~14.2x net leverage vs 4.1x on GAAP basis, the true forward leverage/valuation basis is unresolved and skews bearish.

No segment EBITDA breakout (single reported segment) and no company-adjusted-EBITDA leverage covenant basis disclosed — an expected disclosure gap that obscures which lines actually generate profit; treat as a bearish opacity risk.
TEV/EBITDA is trailing-only with no forward basis at the cross-sectional level; the note flags it cannot distinguish cheap-overshoot from cheap-terminal — a neutral unresolved fact, not directional.
Two CIQ sources disagree on cash ($256M BS vs $223M bridge) and debt ($5,504M BS vs $5,689M bridge); which basis is correct materially affects the equity bridge and is unverified.
The FY26 revenue guide fails its primary-source cross-check (CIQ 2460.0–2485.0 vs release 2.465–2.49) — the reliable current guide is ambiguous.

Covenant maintenance terms and near-term maturity wall are stated as no near-term maturity but the covenant basis is UNKNOWN; whether the below-2.6x deleveraging target is a covenant requirement is unresolved.
Self-funding is MIXED on the two-input read (latest-Q OCF negative, LTM FCF positive) — the Q1 seasonality claim from management is unverified against filings.
Export/data date is a floor (≥2026-06-05), so revision and estimate freshness relative to the June-30 earnings gap-down is uncertain.

caveats: P/E may be distorted by non-recurring EPS — latest annual EPS -20.36 vs recent median 4.71; verify against normalized/forward EPS (CIQ)

Net debt/EBITDA (4.1x) is on REPORTED EBITDA (CIQ / consolidated GAAP), not the covenant basis; management and credit covenants typically define leverage on adjusted EBITDA (a larger denominator → a lower ratio), reconciled in the earnings release/transcript (currently UNAVAILABLE) — do not read 4.1x as the covenant-basis leverage.

business_description.value: Concentrix Corporation designs, builds, and runs integrated customer experience (CX) solutions worldwide. It provides CX process optimization, technology innovation and design engineering, front- and back-office automation, analytics, and business transformation services to clients in various industry verticals comprising technology and consumer electronics; retail, travel, and e-commerce; communications and media; banking, financial services, and insurance; and healthcare. The company also offers customer lifecycle management; CX and user experience strategy and design; data analytics, enterprise intelligence, artificial intelligence readiness, and actionable insights; digital operations, such as B2B sales, performance marketing, customer loyalty, trust and safety, collections, and financial compliance; and GenAI and agentic AI technologies. In addition, it provides digital transformation services that designs and engineer CX solutions to enable efficient customer self-service and build customer loyalty; customer engagement solutions and services that address the entirety of the customer lifecycle; and AI technology that can intelligently act on customer intent to improve customer experience with non-human engagement. Further, the company offers self-service GenAI and agentic AI assistants for applications in data analysis, language translations, and internal chatbots; voice of the customer and analytics solutions to gather and analyze customer feedback; analytics and consulting solutions that synthesize data and provide professional insight to improve clients’ customer experience strategies; specialized support to specific industry verticals; and back office services that support clients in non-customer facing areas. It serves technology and consumer electronics, retail, travel and e-commerce, communications and media, banking, financial services and insurance, healthcare, and other industries. The company was founded in 2004 and is based in Newark, California.
